subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: continuous batching assumptions
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:32:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — follow-up on pricing, token volumes & batching assumptions

Sanjay — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can get pricing aligned with your workload patterns:

- Token profile you shared: ~120M tokens/month initially, scaling to ~600M in 6–9 months; peak concurrency during business hours ~30–50 concurrent requests, average QPS ~8.
- Workload shape: mixture of short chat interactions (~80% of tokens are small responses 20–60 tokens) and occasional long generation (few 400–800 token documents).
- Latency SLOs: 95th < 500ms for chat; for document generation can tolerate up to 2s.
- Key ask: target unit economics — you indicated a target around $250–400 / 1M tokens for hosted inference, subject to batching/concurrency benefits and a pilot.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Attach our preliminary pricing worksheet (Redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf) with three model/replica profiles and a raw cost / 1M token calc.
2) Share a short batching assumptions workbook (batching-assumptions.xlsx) that models continuous batching benefits given your QPS and request-length distribution.
3) Marissa will outline pilot scope and potential reserved throughput options if you want predictable unit economics.

Can you confirm the token volumes above and whether the peak concurrency assumption (30–50) is accurate? Also let me know if your traffic is bursty (large spikes) or relatively steady across the day — that changes continuous batching effectiveness.

If ok, I’ll propose a pilot pricing slice (3 months) and a follow-up call next week to review the workbook.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up on pricing, token volumes & batching assumptions

Stephanie — thanks for the recap and the attachments. Quick confirmations and a few follow-ups:

- Volumes: initial estimate is closer to 100–130M tokens/month for the first quarter, with expected ramp to ~450–600M by Q4 if pilot metrics look good.
- Concurrency/shape: our traffic is fairly steady during 9am–6pm ET (not huge spikes) but we do see predictable peaks when new clinical reports are ingested (daily, short 5–10 minute spikes). Peak concurrent requests are ~35 currently; 50 is a reasonable upper bound for planning.
- Budget range: leadership earmarked $40–60k/month for this project during pilot; we’re aiming for unit economics that land us ~ $300 / 1M tokens or better after batching/optimization.

Questions for you:
1) When you say "continuous batching" — how does that apply to streaming/partial-response workloads? We stream a lot of short chat responses; will we still see batching benefits?
2) Can you show the sensitivity of $/1M tokens to effective batch factor and to target latency?

Happy to hop on a 30m call — Priya (cc) can coordinate. Ideally next Tue/Wed morning ET.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Director of Data Products, Acme Health
Sanjay.Rao@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Pricing — continuous batching sensitivity (internal notes)

Forwarding Sanjay's note with some internal assumptions we should call out before the client call:

- Continuous batching applies to small requests as long as the runtime supports microbatching (we do). For streaming/partial responses, we can still batch tokens at the token generation level when requests align in the KV cache; however, end-to-end latency benefits are smaller than for non-streaming batches. Expect ~10–20% cost reduction from batching alone for heavy streaming workloads versus ~25–40% for request/response patterns where responses are sent after generation.
- Sensitivity: baseline hosted list price (no batching/naive) ~ $700 / 1M tokens for the higher-capacity model profile. With continuous batching and KV cache reuse at the workload profile Sanjay described, we can get to $320–380 / 1M tokens. If they commit to reserved capacity (dedicated pool) and we can tune quantization models, we can push below $300 / 1M.
- Latency tradeoffs: with their 95p < 500ms target, we should keep an eye on batch hold windows. For chat, set microbatch hold to 12–20ms and prioritize low-latency route; that keeps 95p mostly within target while still harvesting batching gains.

Suggested ask on call: get a short sample of request logs (1–2 days) so we can run the batching model and produce a concrete $/1M number. Also propose a 3-month pilot: reserved concurrency baseline 30 qps, burst to 60 qps, and monthly review.

I'll be on the client call to cover pricing details. Camila — can you prepare a slide on microbatch hold tradeoffs and a quick simulation from our batching workbook?

-Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up on pricing, token volumes & batching assumptions

Sanjay — thanks for the clarifications and the budget range. Quick answers and a proposed next step:

1) Continuous batching + streaming: you will see benefits, but smaller than non-streaming. For your traffic mix (80% short chat streaming), model says ~15% expected cost reduction from microbatching and KV reuse. We’ll include that in the workbook sensitivity.

2) Sensitivity: we ran a quick scenario with your 100–130M baseline and the assumed QPS; see summary below (full numbers in attached workbook):
   - Naive hosted (no batching): ~$680 / 1M tokens
   - Hosted with continuous batching (expected): ~$330 / 1M tokens
   - Hosted + reserved throughput (3-month pilot): ~$300 / 1M tokens (commit + small discount)

Pilot proposal:
- Duration: 3 months
- Baseline: 30 qps reserved, burst to 60 qps
- Target price: $300 / 1M tokens for pilot usage (applies up to first 1.5B tokens across the pilot)
- Deliverables: weekly usage reports, batching-effectiveness dashboard, two tuning sessions (model selection/quantization).

If that aligns with your $40–60k/month pilot budget, we can send a short statement of work and a DocuSign to get started. Proposed call: Tue Mar 10, 10am ET — does that work for you?

Link to pilot SoW & signature: https://www.docusign.com/link/ABC123

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
